_comment: Illustrative example for schema documentation only. All numbers, dates and claims are placeholders, not real data or research.
thesis: The concentrate model pushes capital intensity onto bottlers, giving KO high unit economics and a global distribution moat. The main operational exposures are packaging input costs and bottler execution in emerging markets.

strengths.point: Franchise bottlers carry most plant and fleet capex.

risks.point: Aluminum and PET costs pass through bottlers and can squeeze volumes.

invalidation_rationale: Evidence of bottler distress or sustained share loss in key markets would undermine the operational moat.
conviction_reason: The structural advantages are well documented in filings.
self_evidence_reason: Business description and MD&A reviewed; no independent volume data.

sources.title: SEC EDGAR companyfacts - The Coca-Cola Company (CIK 21344)
The Coca-Cola Company - Form 10-K annual reports (SEC EDGAR)

supply_chain.assessment: Concentrate produced in a few plants; packaging and sweetener costs sit mostly with bottlers.

capacity_backlog.assessment: Backlog is not meaningful for a consumer staple; capacity is added by bottlers as volumes grow.

execution.assessment: Refranchising completed in most markets; new product launches are frequent and quickly pruned.

unit_economics.assessment: Concentrate pricing with low capex intensity yields high incremental margins.

operational_moat.assessment: A global bottler network and cooler placement are hard to replicate.
